Report Details

Unconventional: Yes
County: Susquehanna
Municipality: Auburn Twp

Inspection Date: 2020-06-12
Comments: Arrived on location at 08:20. Onsite to initiate a 72 hr. PBUT on all (4) Howell M wells, the 2H, 4H, 6H and 8H wells. I met with Cabot O&G Reps., Devin Lyke, Marshall McCarty, Keenan Small and James Brown. Deven and Marshall were checking and calibrating the transducers on the (20x13), (13x9) and (9x5) annuli of all four wells before starting the PBUT. The (20x13), (13x9) and (9x5) annuli vents were connected together and going to a common poly vent tank (see photo #3), that was shared with the vent lines of the 2H, 4H and 8H wells. There was gas detected at the tank. No gas or flow checks were taken at the block and bleed prier to the the start of the PBUT because of the possibility of commingling. The 2H is temporarily plugged because of stimulation operations at the Powers M pad but the 2H, 4H and 8H wells will remain in production during the PBUT. PBUT was initiated on all wells (20x13), (13x9) and (9x5) annuli at ~ 09:28 on 6/12/20. Left location at 09:35.

Report Details
Inspection Client: DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/19/2026
Violation Code: 102.4(b)1 - EROSION AND SEDIMENT CONTROL REQUIREMENTS - Person conducting earth disturbance activity failed to implement and maintain E & S BMPs to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation.
Violation ID: 8268226
Permit API: 051-21986
Unconventional: No
County: Fayette
Municipality: Redstone Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/19/2026
Comments: On March 19, 2026, the DEP conducted a Follow Up Inspection in response to IRs 4157087, 4157136, 4157162, 4157480, and 4157532. This inspection is separated into 2 inspection reports and discusses 8 observed culverts along the access road as well as any observed erosion and sedimentation issues along the access road. This Inspection Report is Inspection 1 of 2 and assesses Culverts 1-5. All associated violations discussed in both inspection reports are being issued/continued in just this inspection.A COA with the DEP was entered into on 3/07/2019. According to the COA, the Operator shall restore the site within 9 months of plugging. At this time, a rig was on site and plugging operations have commenced.During IRs 4157087/4157136/4157162, the DEP recommended the operator install controls in accordance with the construction sequence and the E and S plan and redline the site plans to appropriately match on-site field changes.During IRs 4157480/4157532, the DEP recommended the operator install CFS along the access road in all sections of E and S off of the access road and above each culvert inlet and outlet, as well as gravel the access road at all culvert crossings in accordance with the E and S plan. The DEP recommended the operator install orange construction fence along the access road near the seep and wetland identified near the culvert 4 inlet and past culvert 5. The DEP recommended the operator restore the roadside ditch at seep.At the time of this inspection, the E and S plan was present in the on-site mailbox at the beginning of the access road. The DEP did not observed any redlining on site plans to depict and appropriately match on-site field changes (Photo 2). The DEP also did not observe the RCE to be installed at the beginning of the access road as depicted on the plans (Photo 1). The access road was also observed to still not be graveled by the operator despite the E and S plan calling for the road to be "graveled as necessary". CFS was observed to be installed at an area where erosion and sedimentation off the access road was previously noted to be located before culvert 1.Observations obtained during today's inspection at culvert crossings 1-5 are as follows:Culvert 1 crossing - culverted for a roadside ditch (Photos 4-7): The outlet still appears to be block. CFS was observed at both the inlet and outlet, however, the CFS at the outlet is improperly installed as complete surface contact to the ground was not observed. Culvert 2 crossing - stream crossing (Photos 8-9): Outlet still appears to be blocked. CFS was observed to be installed and functioning properly at both the inlet and outlet. Culvert 3 crossing - stream crossing (Photos 10-13): The inlet to this culvert appears to still be blocked. CFS was installed at both the inlet and outlet of this culvert, however, the CFS at the inlet is improperly installed as complete contact to the ground was not observed. No sediment was observed to be entering the stream at this time.Culvert 4 crossing - culverted for roadside ditch (Photos 14-17): CFS was observed to be installed at both the inlet and outlet of this culvert, however, the CFS at the inlet is improperly installed as complete contact to the ground was not observed. Culvert still appears to not be receiving water due to operator disturbing channel and causing water to be diverted further down access road. The disturbed channel still appears to be carrying fine sediment towards the stream at culvert 5, however no sediment was observed entering the stream due to the second half of the channel going subsurface with the entry point into the stream unseen (Photos 18-20).Culvert 5 crossing - stream crossing (Photos 21-24): CFS was observed to be installed at both the inlet and outlet of this crossing, however, the CFS at the outlet is improperly installed as complete contact to the ground was not observed. No sediment was observed to be entering the stream at this time.

Comments: On October 7, 2025, the Department conducted an inspection in response to a spill incident at the Alex Paris Well Site. Act 9 sign is present on site. Emergency Response Plan (ERP) is present on site.As outlined in IR 4068219, an estimated 30 gallons of condensate released to the graveled well pad after when a failure occurred on a discharge hose as a contract oil hauler began to load condensate from the production tanks. Specialized Professional Services Inc. (SPSI) responded and remediated the impacted area placing the material into roll-off boxes for disposal.Upon arrival to the site, the Department spoke with Lease Operator Sam Griest, who explained the spill area as the area surrounding the production tanks and secondary containment that has new gravel from approximately the black staircases to the concrete barrier that is spray painted orange. The release reportedly sprayed onto this area and inside the secondary containment. The two roll off boxes remain on site at this time. No staining is observed on the well pad at this time and there is no observable sheen on the fluid inside the secondary containment. Range Resources reportedly remediated the site in accordance with 78a.66(c)(1).Violations for the release are being issued and immediately corrected. The operator is requested to submit a written response within seven (7) days of the receipt of this report. This written response should include an incident report, a timeline of remedial measures, and plan for remediation of the spill or release. The Department is requesting how the operator quantified the amount spilled. The Department also requests the waste manifest from the site remediation be submitted upon receipt.

properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Chief Oil & Gas Llc
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2020-02-24
Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 877793
Permit API: 113-20278
Unconventional: Yes
County: Sullivan
Municipality: Fox Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2020-02-24
Comments: Chief Oil & Gas reported a release of approximately 2 barrels of produced fluid at the Czop Pad on 2/21/20. The release occurred the same day it was reported. I arrived onsite at 10:05 on 2/24/20. I talked with Kellon Balum and Darrin, both of Chief when I arrived. The release occurred when a piece of the B section of the well broke and allowed produced fluid to begin to spray onto the pad (Photo #1, center). This section of the wellhead is not typically used and doesn't receive much gas flow. It usually is used for monitoring certain pressures in the well. It is believed that sand flowing up from the well eroded and weakened a portion of the pipe and allowed it to rupture. Gas, at approximately 700 to 800 psi pushed produced fluid through the opening, about 2 inches in diameter. This mist was somewhat directional but was blown over a large portion of the pad by wind. The release occurred sometime between a crew leaving the site and the site operator, Darrin, arriving. This limits the duration of the release to no more than about 1 hour. Based on the time and rate of release Chief believes approximately 2 barrels of fluid were released. Typically, offsite monitoring equipment is used to detect events such as this, however, equipment was frozen, and the event was undetected. Much of the pad was covered by snow and ice and beginning Friday night (2/21/20) Chief was removing the impacted snow, and excavating the pad as needed (Photo #2). They are continuing to screen with a soil conductivity meter and are removing any impacted soil. The soil is currently on containment and will be covered until containers are brought to the pad and the material is disposed of in a landfill (Photo #3. 4). Due to the volume of the release, Chief is required to pursue site remediation in accordance with 25 Pa. Code § 78a.66(c). The result of this inspection is Violations noted.

Comments: On 4/09/2026, the Department conducted a Compliance Schedule Evaluation (CSE) inspection of Diversified's Myers 12 plugged well site located in Springhill Township, Fayette County.According to Department records, this well was plugged on 5/12/2025. Therefore the well site restoration was due by 2/12/2026. A Well Site Restoration Report (WSRR) was due by 4/12/2026. A Well Site Extension Request submitted by the operator on 12/19/2025 was returned by the Department (IR 4125566). No WSRR has been received to-date from the operator for this site. A CO and A was entered into between the Department and Diversified on 3/07/2019. According to the CO and A, Diversified is to restore the Well Site in accordance with Section 3216 of the 2012 Oil and Gas Act, 58 Pa. C.S.A. 3216.The following was observed during the inspection:The former access road and well site have not yet achieved 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth coverage. Light erosion rills were observed in the access road. Temporary Erosion and Sedimentation (E and S) Controls remain installed on site. The E and S/Restoration plans are available in a mailbox at the former site entrance. They are deteriorated, but remain legible.No surface fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near the approximate location of the plugged well. No plugging monument was observed during this inspection.Based on observations from this inspection, the well site and access road are not restored. The Department recommended in IR 4125566 that the Operator fully restore the well site and access road 2/12/2026 and submit a WSRR by 4/12/2026. However, no Post-Plugging WSRR has been received from the operator. Therefore, a violation shall be issued for failure to restore the well site and access road in accordance with the 3/07/2019 CO and A.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 944927
Permit API: 015-23674
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Franklin Twp
Inspection Type: Administrative/File Review
Inspection Date: 2/11/2022
Comments: This Inspection Report cites violations for an apparent flowback (brine) release to the pad surface. The Analytical Report (attached) for SAC 942 metals shows 16.7 mg/L barium and 80.6 mg/L strontium in the liquid sample collected on February 1, 2022 (inspection 3315684). The narrative and findings in this report are from that previous inspection. I spoke with Justin Myers (Chief) on site. He explained that Cudd started drilling out plugs from the 5 Marcellus well heads today. They will have 3 coil tubing units on site to complete this job. Myers expects they will finish drilling the plugs in about 10 days. Workers are removing liner containment used while hydraulically fracturing the 5 Marcellus wells at this site. Pooled liquid on the south half of the pad surface has electrical conductivity of 14.1 - >19.99 mS/cm with an Oakton PCSTestr 35. I collected liquid sample 0935-430 in a 125 mL bottle and sent it to the DEP lab for SAC 942 metals analysis. The puddles across the south end of the pad are relatively shallow (<1/2" deep), so I did not fill a 500 mL bottle for inorganic element analysis. Violations could be cited pending laboratory sample analysis. Myers contacted Brendon Logan (Chief) to investigate the pooled liquid on the pad surface. I did not observe accelerated erosion or sedimentation during this inspection. Post Construction Stormwater Management (PCSM) controls are in place and appear to be functioning as designed. Air temp 26F JLP

Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 920538
Permit API: 059-24935
Unconventional: Yes
County: Greene
Municipality: Greene Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 6/09/2021
Comments: Prior to inspection: On 6/2/21 Range Resource's Derek Zofchak reported a produced water spill estimated at 15 gallons resulting from a pump operator "overfilling a tub" during site activities. The spill did not reportedly impact or threaten the Waters of the Commonwealth but extended roughly 60' off the site and down a fill slope. On 6/9/21 an incident inspection of the Indian Point Unit 1 Well Pad was conducted in response to an operator reported spill (CTS ID: 357202). The following was observed: >>Communication with the operator in conjunction with the inspection indicated that the spill had been fully remediated and a roll off box of impacted material was taken for disposal. >>Work crews were on site at the time of inspection adding compost filter sock (CFS) and conducting site maintenance. (Photo #1) >>An erosion channel was noted leading to the well pad near the juncture of the site access road and the pad. Remediation and stabilization are recommended. (Photo #2) >>The site was reportedly being prepared for upgrades with numerous liners, tanks and other equipment, and earth work noted. The site is less than five acres and does not appear to ever have/need an ESCGP. (Photo #3) >>Background conductivity readings as measured in several areas less than ten feet off pad were between 0.15-0.20mS. (Photo #4) >>In general conductivity readings around the pad area where between 0.4-0.8mS which may be related to pad materials (limestone) or residual impact. (Photo #5) >>The remediated spill area appeared to be as described by the operator with conductivity readings at background levels. (Photo #6) >>An area of saturated soil roughly 10'x5' near the pad liner/containment and directly adjacent to the remediated primary spill area was also significantly impacted with conductivity readings of 8.5-9.2mS. This may indicate additional spilled production fluids having leaked under the pad liner and panels. Follow up inspection needed once liner and pads are moved. The findings, a request for notification when the expanded spill area is accessible, and the need for follow up inspections were immediately communicated to Range Resources' Dennis Furmanek and Derek Zofchak. (Photo #7-8) >>Determination: The initially reported spill and the identified area of residual impact constitute violations of 25 Pa. Code § 78a.54, 25 Pa. Code § 78a.57(a), and 35 P.S. § 6018.301 in that the operator failed to control regulated materials in a manner that prevents pollution to the ground and Waters of the Commonwealth.

properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Chesapeake Appalachia Llc
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2019-03-27
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 845144
Permit API: 113-20411
Unconventional: Yes
County: Sullivan
Municipality: Cherry Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2019-03-27
Comments: I received at call at 07:30 from Eric Hottenstein of Chesapeake to inform the Department of a release of oil-based drilling mud. He then told me that he would also call the main number to report the spill. I arrived onsite at 09:25 and met with Eric Hottenstein and Nick Krut, both of Chesapeake. We went to observe the release and they described what had occurred. Some newer wells on the pad were recently stimulated and were being set up for flowback. These wells had the intermediate annulus plumbed to a sentry valve (Photo #1). The valves are designed to vent to prevent a build up of pressure. It is believed that the mechanism inside this valve may have become stuck and allowed a build up of pressure causing the top of the valve to come off and release oil-based drilling mud. The area around the wells was partially covered by secondary containment. A section had been removed around the older wells on the site in order to perform maintenance. The unprotected area consisted of both the gravel pad surface and the cement apron around the older wells (Photos #3 & 6). The released drilling mud coated parts of the 105H well, secondary containment, gravel pad, older wells, and cement apron. Eric and Nick believed that a total of 42 gallons of drilling mud was released with 21 gallons on containment and 21 gallons off containment. Before I arrived Mountain Energy was already onsite and had used a Super Sucker to remove the free portion of the drilling mud. They were in the process of power washing the apron and allowing the water/mud mixture to drain into the well cellars (Photo #7). The well heads were going to be washed next with water and degreaser. The well cellars are cement lined and should be sealed to allow the collected water to be vacuumed out. The gravel portion was going to be scraped and excavated as needed. Chesapeake also mentioned pulling back some of the remaining secondary containment to remove and mud that may have seeped underneath. The 105H annulus was connected to a day tank (approx. 350 gallon poly tank) that was in secondary containment. This was a precautionary measure in the event of a second release. Crews were also onsite installing flowback equipment and checking the annulus pressure gauges to monitor the situation. Eric believed the area would be cleaned in about 2 hours. He also mentioned that the day tanks may be installed on other wells in the future to prevent another release. Violations noted.

The unprotected area consisted of both the gravel pad surface and the cement apron around the older wells (Photos #3 & 6). The released drilling mud coated parts of the 105H well, secondary containment, gravel pad, older wells, and cement apron. Eric and Nick believed that a total of 42 gallons of drilling mud was released with 21 gallons on containment and 21 gallons off containment. Before I arrived Mountain Energy was already onsite and had used a Super Sucker to remove the free portion of the drilling mud. They were in the process of power washing the apron and allowing the water/mud mixture to drain into the well cellars (Photo #7). The well heads were going to be washed next with water and degreaser. The well cellars are cement lined and should be sealed to allow the collected water to be vacuumed out. The gravel portion was going to be scraped and excavated as needed. Chesapeake also mentioned pulling back some of the remaining secondary containment to remove and mud that may have seeped underneath. The 105H annulus was connected to a day tank (approx. 350 gallon poly tank) that was in secondary containment. This was a precautionary measure in the event of a second release. Crews were also onsite installing flowback equipment and checking the annulus pressure gauges to monitor the situation. Eric believed the area would be cleaned in about 2 hours. He also mentioned that the day tanks may be installed on other wells in the future to prevent another release. Violations noted.

An onsite meeting was scheduled with Petro Erie Inc. and the Department which developed this Inspection Report.Individuals present at the onsite meeting:Harry Rhoades -Owner/Operator of Petro Erie Inc.Chris Rhoades -Driver for Harry RhoadesRob Bechtel -PA DEPRick Willey -PA DEPAlan Wolf -PA DEPLucas Eichner -PA DEPSteve Wells -PA DEPThe meeting was started off by Rob Bechtel stating the reason for the meeting and what was discovered during a previous site inspection on 7/21/2023 with violations cited. It was discussed that there is a potential that the discharge of produced fluid from the tank battery may have impacted the Reno, PA public water supply. Mr. Rhoades asked if the pubic water supply was now safe to drink and if regular testing was being conducted. We informed him that the oil and gas program was collecting samples for analysis to determine if the water supply was impacted by oil and gas activity and that the Safe Drinking Water program was working with Venango Water Company related to the public water supply. The discussion with Mr. Rhoades made him aware of the fact that there are more than several concerns with his lease. The Department recommended that he hire an environmental consultant to help him through the cleanup and reporting process of an Act 2 cleanup regarding the discharge of produced fluid and the potential impact of the Reno public water supply. Other violations were discussed regarding the other wells on his lease. Statements that were made by Mr. Rhoades during the meeting:-He is the only owner/operator of Petro Erie Inc-He pumps the wells on the lease himself-One well on the lease is on a timer and pumps when he is not present-Mr. Rhoades does not know what occurred at the site referring to the discharge of produced fluid-Wants the water of the households in Reno tested-Hauled 3 loads of brine, 1 load hauled by Gavin to disposal in OH and 2 loads hauled by Paul Weaver to a frac job in West Virginia-Stated that the tank battery and the impact area was present when he purchased the lease

Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a follow-up inspection of Seneca Resource's Peffer Strong 483 well site located in Sullivan Township, Tioga County on 9/6/2022 at 1120 hours. The weather was 67 degrees with cloudy skies. Rain fell onsite within the past 24 hours. During today's inspection, a section of the secondary containment structure located in the center of the pad was overtopping with fluid. A sheen was observed atop the fluid that was observed overtopping the secondary containment wall. Sample 0983-345 was collected from the fluid located just outside of the overtopping containment wall (photo #5). Fluids held in the center of the pad overtopping the containment that was field measured ranged from 320 to 430us/cm. 25 Pa. Code 78a.64a.(e) states "Operator failed to remove stormwater as soon as possible and prior to the capacity of secondary containment being reduced by 10% or more." Areas where elevated conductivity pad material and fluid were discovered in a 6/23/2022 inspection report were reevaluated today. Pooled fluids located near the entrance were now field measured at a range of 480 to 840us/cm. Elevated conductivity pad material located in front of the produced water tanks' offload area was now field measured at a range of 0.2 to 0.3mS/cm. The area located just southeast of the Gas Processing Units (GPUs) secondary containment (photo #6) where elevated conductivity pad material was discovered on 6/23/2022 is now retaining fluid that was field measured at ~3.72mS/cm. Sample 0983-344 was collected from this fluid. Just east of this area, a rock-lined stormwater channel was retaining fluid that was field measured at ~2.30mS/cm today. Sample 0983-343 was collected from the rock-lined channel (photo #8). Based on the findings of today's inspection, violations of the following cited against API #117-22110 cited on 7/7/2022 remain outstanding at this time:25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a)35 P.S. 6018.30135 P.S. 691.402(b)In addition, a violation of the following is also cited against API #117-22110 at this time:25 Pa. Code 78a.64a(e)Additional violations are pending, awaiting sample results 0983-343, 344, and 345. I departed the site at 1255 hours.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Code: 91.34(A) - ACTIVITIES UTILIZING POLLUTANTS - Failure to take necessary measures to prevent the substances from directly or indirectly reaching waters of this Commonwealth, through accident, carelessness, maliciousness, hazards of weather or from another cause.
Violation ID: 8261774
Permit API: 129-29235
Unconventional: Yes
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Penn Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 1/13/2026
Comments: On January 13 2026, the Department conducted an incident inspection at the Aphrodite Well Site (ESCGP issued on 5/9/2020, amended on 2/5/2024, expiring on 2/4/2029) in regards to a release reported to the Department on 1/12/2026 (CTS 394575). Present during the inspection was operator representative Justin Miller.The findings are as follows:At the time of the inspections, the Act 9 sign was present and appeared to be installed in accordance with 78a55. The Emergency Response Plan (ERP), Preparedness, Prevention and Contingency (PPC) plan (which contained all required components) and site plans were present in the onsite mailbox. The access road appeared stabilized with gravel.At the time of inspection, there are 5 total wells on the well pad. According to the operator, stimulation for all 5 wells has been completed and they are preparing to conduct drill outs and flowback operations over the next 3 weeks.Upon inspection, it appeared the stimulation equipment was being demobilized. The drilling equipment still onsite appeared to be within secondary containment. The secondary containment appeared to be installed correctly with no tears or leaks. During the inspection, Mr. Miller guided the Department to the location of the reported release. According to Mr. Miller the release occurred on 1/13/2026. He stated the release occurred from a loose hose connection from one of the tanks. At the time of the inspection the operator is estimating a total release of 15 gallons of a produced water was released to the graveled well pad.The Department observed the location of the spill and remediation. It appeared the area of the spill was in an approximate 4 foot by 20 foot area outside of the secondary containment for the tanks next to a GPU. Conductivity readings including several readings of OR (Over Detectable Range, >20MS) , 11.46mS, and 1.57mS, were obtained in the area of the release. During the inspection, the Department observed 2 small areas of excavation. Mr. Miller stated that additional excavation will occur as needed when the containment is removed from its location.The operator is requested to submit a written response within seven (7) days of the receipt of this report. This written response should include an incident report, a timeline of remedial measures, and plan for remediation of the spill or release.The Department is requesting how the operator quantified the amount spilled. The Department also requests the waste manifest from the site remediation be submitted upon receipt.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued against the Aphodite 2M well for the observed release.

Comments: Water samples collected on 5/28/2019 at the XTO Energy PA Tract 8546 Pad A as part of Complaint No. 342466, documented in Inspection Report 2886516, were received on 6/28/2019. The results indicate the seep off the West edge of the pad contained elevated levels of chloride and strontium, which indicates the fluid was a pollutional substance. Results from a sample of the same seep, collected by XTO Energy on 5/16/2019 and received on 7/3/2019 from XTO Energy, are consistent with the Department's results. The release of a pollutional substance outside of containment are a violation of section 402(b) of the Clean Streams Law, 78a.56(a), and Section 301 of the Solid Waste Management Act. The failure to report the release of a pollutional substance is a violation of 78a.66(b). Due to the unknown extent, material, and volume of the release, the Department recommends that XTO Energy remediate under Act 2.

Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 861838
Permit API: 121-44938
Unconventional: No
County: Venango
Municipality: Pinegrove Twp
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 2019-09-10
Comments: Onsite for a spill response that was reported by the operator. The release occurred near the Hart 3 well. It is believed that there was a failure in a fitting along the pipeline that allowed the leak to occur, but was not excavated yet. The operator has hired a clean-up contractor (ECS&R)) who was onsite investigating the extent of the release and removing crude oil from the watercourse. The crude oil pushed to the surface at the Hart 3 well and there is oil that has traveled over the ground near the well. It also appears oil has traveled subsurface possibly in a trench for the electric. There is oil seeping out underneath a culvert approximately 100 feet north west. The oil continues to follow the watercourse in a northwest direction for approximately another 200 feet. The contractors are setting up defensive measures to prevent oil from entering a pond that is fed by the watercourse. The pond is located approximately 50 feet past the last visible oil. Contractor intends to remain onsite removing oil from the watercourse and continue in investigate the extent of the release. Violations are noted.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 9/14/2021
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 929655
Permit API: 015-21152
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Sheshequin Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 9/15/2021
Comments: The DEP conducted an incident inspection of Chesapeake's Covington well site located in Sheshequin Township, Bradford County on 9/14/2021 at 1340 hours. The weather was 78 degrees with partly cloudy skies. The inspection was conducted in response to a release of produced water reported to the DEP by Chesapeake. Numerous Chesapeake representatives were on location when I arrived. Chesapeake representatives explained that a connection on the dump line of the GPU onsite had failed, causing the release of produced water into the containment skid of the GPU and then onto the pad surface. Fluid held in the containment skid of the GPU was field measured at Over Ranged (>19.99mS/cm)(photo #2). Damp areas on the both sides of the GPU (photos #3 & 4) were observed and the pad material was determined to be elevated for electrical conductivity and field measured at >4.00mS/cm. The release appears to have migrated towards the area located behind the GPU fenced-in area (photo #7). Soil screenings in this area were also elevated (>4.00mS/cm). A small puddle of water had collected against the earthen containment berm of the pad, behind the GPU (photo #10) and was field measured at Over Range (>19.99mS/cm). The area of impact was roughly estimated at 50 feet x 40 feet. Chesapeake planned to dispatch Creston Environmental to conduct screening and sampling. A plan to remove the GPU in order to begin excavation was put in place. Violations of the following are cited against API #015-21152 at this time: 35 P.S. 691.402(b) 25 Pa. Code 78a.57(a) 35 P.S. 6018.301 I departed the site at 1420 hours.

Comments: Onsite for a spill response that was reported by the operator. The release occurred near the Hart 3 well. It is believed that there was a failure in a fitting along the pipeline that allowed the leak to occur, but was not excavated yet. The operator has hired a clean-up contractor (ECS&R)) who was onsite investigating the extent of the release and removing crude oil from the watercourse. The crude oil pushed to the surface at the Hart 3 well and there is oil that has traveled over the ground near the well. It also appears oil has traveled subsurface possibly in a trench for the electric. There is oil seeping out underneath a culvert approximately 100 feet north west. The oil continues to follow the watercourse in a northwest direction for approximately another 200 feet. The contractors are setting up defensive measures to prevent oil from entering a pond that is fed by the watercourse. The pond is located approximately 50 feet past the last visible oil. Contractor intends to remain onsite removing oil from the watercourse and continue in investigate the extent of the release. Violations are noted.

Comments: This inspection is in response to a complaint of a spill on 03/07/2022 located at the Armac lease on Bauer Hill road. The complainant reported a strong smell and saw diapers and oil booms in the Bauer Hill road ditch as well as inside the containment diking. Upon responding to the complaint, and speaking with Vince Bailey the pumper for the lease he reported that the storage tank had over flowed on Saturday March 5th, he cleaned up the oil inside containment he estimated the spill at 2.5 barrels. Monday crude oil had breached the diking by migrating through the pervious material used in the construction of the containment. The crude oil flowed down slope approx 250 feet into a road side ditch on Bauer Hill road, it continued another 275 feet into an unnamed tributary (UNT) of Glade Run. There was evidence of crude along the tributary to its confluence of Glad Run. An unknown amount of crude oil was released and made its way into waters of the Commonwealth.

Report Details

Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2020-02-24
Comments: On February 24, 2020 , DEP representative Brad Kline conducted an inspection for a reported spill (CTS at 348187) at Beech Resources Premier Well Pad. At the time of inspection, the operator was in the process of rigging down the site from the recent stimulation of the wells onsite. The DEP met with Don Stevenson of Beech Resources. He explained that some hoses were disconnected from the blender and were not drained of production fluid. The hoses were not completely placed on containment and spilled about 30 gallons of brine water outside of containment. The operator was in the process of vacuuming the containment. Once that has been completed the containment will be removed and the excavation of the impacted area will begin. Penn E&R is scheduled to collect biased samples of the impacted area. DEP conducted field screening of the puddles in the area where the hoses spilled the brine water for conductivity. The puddles tested returned an over range reading of the conductivity meter (>19.99 mS/cm). Beech Resources plans to excavate the impacted soil to below a soil conductivity of 1000 uS/cm. February 25, 2020 The DEP received an email from Don Stevenson with pictures showing the excavation of the impacted area from the spill the evening of 2/24/2020. The DEP followed up with a site visit to confirm the excavation. At the time of the visit, Penn E&R was onsite continuing the conductivity delineation of the spill. The operator was also continuing to excavate impacted soil from the spill. The area that has been excavated is about a 20' x 30' area at a depth of less than a foot. Penn E&R stated that five 10 yard roll off dumpsters have been filled with impacted soil to this point. More excavation is going to be required to remove the remaining impacted soil. The DEP screened the area of the spill, which resulted in a range of 200 uS/cm to areas that were over range of the meter(>4.00 mS/cm). Before leaving the well pad, the DEP spoke with Don Stevenson on the phone and explained with the area excavated and the amount of impacted soil collected that the DEP recommends starting the Act 2 process. The spill of production fluid from the hoses outside of containment is a violation of the Clean Streams Law 402(b), §78a.56(a), and Solid Waste Management Act Section 301.

Comments: This inspection report has been developed to document an incident response inspection that was conducted on-site.Kris Bowser with AMS Energy contacted me on Thursday, July 14, 2022, to report a brine spill that had occurred on AMS's Barrett Pattison 5 Well Site. The spill had been discovered earlier the same day. A valve had been broken off of a fiberglass brine tank that was used on-site. Kris believed that the valve had likely been damaged by an ATV that had gotten too close to the tank. Fluid from the tank had recently been hauled out. Kris estimated that less than a barrel of brine had been spilled onto the ground near the tank.Kris met me on-site to view the spill. The damaged valve had been repaired. Most of the spilled brine appeared to have settled in a swale that ran next to the tank. The impacted area was clearly marked with dead vegetation. My soil conductivity probe was used to verify the extent of the impacted area. Elevated readings were not observed beyond the area marked by the dead vegetation. A plan for addressing the impacted soil was discussed with Kris. The soil should be excavated and hauled to a landfill. Kris indicated the AMS would provide the Department with a receipt of disposal from the landfill once the soil has been disposed of.

All diesel tanks observed onsite to power heavy machinery were held in containment (photo #9).Site stabilization could not be adequately assessed due to snow coverage.
